family.description: This entry represents animal bestrophin homologues. Bestrophin is a 68-kDa basolateral plasma membrane protein expressed in retinal pigment epithelial cells (RPE). It is encoded by the VMD2 gene, which is mutated in Best macular dystrophy, a disease characterised by a depressed light peak in the electrooculogram [[cite:PUB00011865]]. VMD2 encodes a 585-amino acid protein with an approximate mass of 68 kDa which has been designated bestrophin. Bestrophin shares homology with the Caenorhabditis elegans RFP gene family, named for the presence of a conserved arginine (R), phenylalanine (F), proline (P), amino acid sequence motif. Bestrophin is a plasma membrane protein, localised to the basolateral surface of RPE cells consistent with a role for bestrophin in the generation or regulation of the EOG light peak. Bestrophin and other RFP family members represent a new class of chloride channels, indicating a direct role for bestrophin in generating the light peak [[cite:PUB00011865]]. The VMD2 gene underlying Best disease was shown to represent the first human member of the RFP-TM protein family. More than 97% of the disease-causing mutations are located in the N-terminal RFP-TM domain implying important functional properties [[cite:PUB00011864]]. The bestrophins are four-pass transmembrane chloride-channel proteins [[cite:PUB00096747]], and the RFP-TM or bestrophin domain extends from the N-terminus through approximately 350 amino acids and contains all of the TM domains as well as nearly all reported disease causing mutations [[cite:PUB00109156]]. Interestingly, the RFP motif is not conserved evolutionarily back beyond Metazoa, neither is it in plant members.
family.name: Bestrophin, RFP-TM, chloride channel

causal_graphs.context: 2016 Figure 1B-D representative same-bilayer comparison. Symmetric 30 mM KCl, 20 mM HEPES-NaOH pH 7.6, 0.21 mM EGTA and 0.19 mM CaCl2 initially give about 300 nM free calcium; 3:1 wt/wt POPE/POPG, 22-24 C. Add 10 mM EGTA to both sides. Currents at +100 mV are averaged over the final 200 ms of a 2-s pulse; empty-bilayer currents are subtracted.

evidence.explanation: Figure 1B-D and the electrophysiology Methods support the bilateral EGTA comparison. These displayed traces are from one representative bilayer, not separate independent replicates.
Archived sequence, current mapping and deposited construct agree over the tested region; their full-length sequences are not identical. This is identity support, not an additional causal experiment.

edges.mechanism: Chelating calcium on both sides strongly reduces the current under the same bilayer and voltage conditions. The effect supports calcium-dependent activity without directly resolving calcium-binding or neck-motion microsteps.
edges.subject: bilateral-egta-in-wt-bilayer

causal_graphs.family_mapping: Historical E1C3A0 is deleted, but its archived sequence and current A0A8V0ZZU7 match exactly at 1-405; PF01062 spans 1-324 inclusive. Five full-length differences lie beyond 405. PDB 4RDQ entity 1 exactly matches current residues 2-405 plus EGEEF, consistent with the cited purification's MS/Edman-confirmed Thr2 start. Other mutant clone sequences are not independently reconstructed.
causal_graphs.limitations: This is a direct current endpoint after chelation, not an observed atomic gate-closing trajectory. Both channel orientations are present; bilateral chelation is not interchangeable with one-sided treatment. The construct extends beyond the Pfam profile and does not prove isolated-domain sufficiency or a universal family calcium threshold.

nodes.label: Add 10 mM EGTA to both sides of the WT BEST1 bilayer

causal_graphs.scope: Chicken BEST1 encoded residues 1-405 plus C-terminal EGEEF, expressed in Pichia and reconstituted in planar bilayers. Not the full 762-aa protein, human retinal cells or bacterial KpBest.
causal_graphs.title: Bilateral calcium chelation decreases purified chicken BEST1 current

causal_graphs.context: Symmetric 30 mM KCl, POPE/POPG 3:1, pH 7.6, 22-24 C. After adding 10 mM EGTA to cis, trans solutions use 1 mM EGTA/calcium-EGTA mixtures to vary free calcium from near zero to 350 nM. Current magnitude at -100 mV is normalized to the 350-nM response. Three separate bilayers, SEM; two-second pulses and final 200-ms averaging.

evidence.explanation: Figure 1E/F and trans-perfusion Methods support reactivation with the stated orientation and normalization controls.

edges.mechanism: Increasing free calcium on the trans side restores current magnitude in the accessible channel orientation, while the cis-facing population remains silenced. The normalized electrophysiological response is not an independently measured binding isotherm.
edges.subject: trans-calcium-increase-with-cis-egta

causal_graphs.family_mapping: E1C3A0 archived 1-405 matches current A0A8V0ZZU7 exactly; PF01062 is 1-324. The purified construct includes the EGEEF tag and processing to Thr2 established in the cited original method; it is not full-length BEST1 or an isolated Pfam fragment.
causal_graphs.limitations: The fitted half-response concentration of 17 +/- 3 nM is assay-specific and is not a directly measured calcium-binding Kd. Increasing current magnitude at a fixed negative voltage does not imply a universal direction of chloride flow. No atomic motion, stoichiometric binding event or human disease mechanism is directly tracked.

nodes.label: Increase trans free calcium while cis remains chelated
Normalized BEST1 current magnitude at -100 mV

causal_graphs.scope: Purified tagged chicken BEST1 1-405 in the 2016 Figure 1E/F bilayer protocol. The cis-side population remains silenced during trans perfusion.
causal_graphs.title: Trans-side calcium restores BEST1 current after orientation-selective silencing

causal_graphs.context: Standard symmetric 30 mM KCl solutions with about 300 nM free calcium, 20 mM HEPES-NaOH pH 7.6, POPE/POPG 3:1 and 22-24 C. DIDS is added to both sides through 1 mM with one minute mixing. Current magnitude at -100 mV is normalized to no DIDS. Three experiments; up to 2% DMSO vehicle does not noticeably alter current.

evidence.explanation: Figure 1I/J and DIDS Methods support the dose-dependent current decrease and vehicle qualification.

edges.mechanism: DIDS lowers the measured current magnitude in a concentration-dependent comparison, with the solvent control retained. No specific molecular binding or pore-blocking geometry is directly established.
edges.subject: bilateral-dids-addition

causal_graphs.family_mapping: The E1C3A0 experimental region 1-405 exactly matches A0A8V0ZZU7 and contains PF01062 at 1-324. The EGEEF-tagged, processed construct is distinguished from the full-length reference and other bestrophins.
causal_graphs.limitations: Current inhibition does not identify a DIDS binding site, unique gating mechanism or therapeutic effect. Dose-response fits depend on this preparation and are not family-wide constants. No precise drug affinity is assigned.

nodes.label: DIDS added to both sides of the calcium-containing BEST1 bilayer
BEST1 current magnitude relative to the no-DIDS condition

causal_graphs.scope: Tagged chicken BEST1 1-405 in the 2016 Figure 1I/J planar bilayer experiment, not drug treatment of retinal cells.
causal_graphs.title: DIDS decreases purified BEST1 current in the bilayer assay

causal_graphs.context: Symmetric 30 mM KCl bilayers, POPE/POPG 3:1, pH 7.6, 22-24 C, initially about 300 nM free calcium. Add 10 mM EGTA to both sides and stir four minutes. Current at +100 mV after chelation is normalized to each construct's calcium-present current. Three separate bilayers per comparison, SEM.

evidence.explanation: Figure 3C TripleA versus WT normalized fractions, corroborated by Figure 3A/B I-V curves, support the directed comparison.

edges.mechanism: The joint TripleA construct retains nearly all of its calcium-present current after chelation, unlike WT. This measures reduced calcium dependence without proving each individual substitution independently causes the joint phenotype.
edges.subject: triplea-neck-substitution

evidence.explanation: Figure 3C F80A and WT bars support the normalized retained-fraction increase under matched protocols.

edges.mechanism: F80A retains a larger fraction of its own calcium-present current than WT after chelation. Partial retention is not complete calcium independence or proof of an increased absolute transport rate.
edges.subject: f80a-neck-substitution

evidence.explanation: Figure 3C F80N versus WT is the adopted comparison, not a simulated wetting trajectory.

edges.mechanism: F80N retains a greater fraction of current than WT after calcium chelation. A hydrophilic substitution effect supports altered regulation but does not directly observe pore wetting or a particular structural motion.
edges.subject: f80n-neck-substitution

causal_graphs.family_mapping: I76, F80 and F84 are verified in the identical historical/current 1-405 region of E1C3A0/A0A8V0ZZU7 and within PF01062 residues 1-324. TripleA is one joint perturbation, not three independently sufficient mutations.
causal_graphs.limitations: Normalized retained fraction is not absolute current, single-channel conductance or open probability; precise incorporation is unknown. F80I is described as nearly WT-like in calcium dependence relative to the larger mutant effects and is not assigned an all-or-none independence edge. Neck mutations do not substantially switch anion/cation selectivity. Structural gate and quadrupole models are interpretations, not directly observed trajectories.

nodes.label: Joint I76A/F80A/F84A TripleA instead of WT
Fraction of calcium-present current retained after EGTA

causal_graphs.scope: Individual F80A/F80N and joint I76A/F80A/F84A TripleA constructs of tagged chicken BEST1 1-405, compared with WT in 2016 Figure 3C.
causal_graphs.title: Neck substitutions increase the current fraction retained after calcium chelation

causal_graphs.context: 0.1 mg/ml protein and 10 mg/ml POPE/POPG before 100-fold dilution; internal 100 mM Na2SO4, 10 mM HEPES pH 8.2, 1 mM EGTA. External 125 mM NaCl and calcium-EGTA give about 2 uM free calcium. CCCP initiates ACMA quench coupled to anion influx. The cited 2014 method supplies 2 uM ACMA, 1 uM CCCP, 0.5 mg/ml BSA and external pH 8.1. Comparisons were purified/reconstituted in parallel and assayed on the same day.

evidence.explanation: Figure 4A/C calcium-present traces show the WT versus clasp-mutant flux-associated signal difference. The small residual drift is not claimed to be an independently resolved zero flux.
The original method cited by the 2016 paper supplies dye/ionophore details and the coupled nature of the fluorescence readout, not a new 2016 control or an independent replicate.

edges.mechanism: The joint clasp substitution reduces the quench observed under externally supplied calcium relative to WT. This is a measured coupled flux effect, not direct proof that a particular calcium-coordination bond was broken.
edges.subject: d301a-d304a-clasp-substitution

evidence.explanation: Figure 4C/D compares the double mutant with the combined five-site mutant. Calcium-free traces are additional context, not silently merged into this condition.

edges.mechanism: Adding the joint TripleA substitution to the clasp-mutant background restores strong quench under the adopted calcium-present condition. Genetic coupling of these regions is supported without a directly observed sequence of conformational movements or independent sufficiency of each substitution.
edges.subject: triplea-added-to-clasp-mutant

causal_graphs.family_mapping: D301/D304 and I76/F80/F84 lie within A0A8V0ZZU7 PF01062 residues 1-324 and the experimentally mapped 1-405 construct. The 2014 purification confirms Thr2 processing and the deposited sequence matches residues 2-405 plus EGEEF. Complete 2016 mutant clone sequences remain unverified.
causal_graphs.limitations: ACMA reports coupled acidification, not direct chloride concentration or a tracked molecular gate. The 2016 traces do not specify exact replicate count or recording temperature; bilayer temperature is not borrowed. Empty vesicles were prepared but are not displayed in Figure 4. Size-exclusion similarity does not eliminate every folding/incorporation alternative. Outside-only calcium activates only the appropriate orientation; this can affect WT/mutant flux comparisons.

nodes.label: Add joint I76A/F80A/F84A to the D301A/D304A background

causal_graphs.scope: D301A/D304A compared with WT, and the joint TripleA/D301A/D304A construct compared with D301A/D304A, in 2016 Figure 4A/C/D proteoliposomes. Only the external 2-uM-calcium condition is adopted here.
causal_graphs.title: Clasp substitutions reduce coupled chloride flux and TripleA restores it

discussions.notes: Resolve exact mutant clones, flux replicate/temperature details and incorporation controls. Assess later inactivation (PMID:30237227), cryo-EM gating (PMID:30628889) and GABA activation (PMID:40249777) as additional primary contexts, not already reviewed edges.
